profile.reading:
This is Digital Realty facility SFO10, at 200 Paul Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94124. Digital Realty's own property listing for SFO10, fetched this session, lists the building at 495,000 square feet.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building sits within Digital Realty's San Francisco Bay Area footprint, which includes carrier-dense downtown San Francisco buildings and additional sites across the East Bay. Digital Realty markets its Bay Area properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, Silicon Valley, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform. The company does not publish a consolidated IT power rating in megawatts for individual San Francisco buildings in the sources reviewed this session.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage, with the San Francisco Bay Area figuring among the company's longest-held US metros dating back to its original public listing in 2004.

San Francisco's Article 20 and related planning rules have shaped where new large-load facilities can be sited downtown, a factor local coverage has tied to the concentration of legacy carrier-hotel and colocation buildings like this one in the SoMa and Mission Bay areas rather than newer suburban construction.

reading.body:
Digital Realty SFO10 is a 495,000 square foot colocation building at 200 Paul Avenue in San Francisco, operated by Digital Realty as a wholesale landlord facility that does not itself run compute workloads. The company does not publish an IT power capacity figure for this individual building; its FY2025 Form 10-K discloses only aggregate capacity and facility counts by region rather than per-building power ratings. Without a published megawatt figure, the capacity of this site cannot be calculated from the data available.

The building sits within Digital Realty's San Francisco Bay Area footprint, one of the company's longest-standing US markets, anchored by carrier-dense downtown San Francisco properties positioned as interconnection hubs. The Bay Area region overall hosts large compute campuses for Google, Meta, and other tenants tracked elsewhere in this registry, served by PG&E. Of 103 mapped data center facilities across California, only 11 publish IT power capacity; the state total is 365 megawatts of published capacity across all operators, making it a fragmented market in terms of disclosed power draw.

SFO10's relevance to AI scaling depends on tenant commitments not disclosed in operator publications. As a colocation landlord, Digital Realty's value lies in interconnection density and power availability rather than scale; San Francisco's local land-use rules have concentrated new large-load facilities in older carrier-hotel sites rather than enabling expansions that might otherwise occur. Whether this building supplies power to AI workloads, and at what density, is not published.
